- Both zero values reproduce baseline pixels; Saturation −100 produces equal working neutral channels within the chosen neutral-axis tolerance and preserves alpha.
- Test a brightness sweep from near black through 16× reference white and hue sweeps across the full circle; no NaNs, abrupt hue shifts, or clipping of the master.
- Vibrance measurably applies its documented weighting; record hue/luminance errors against fixed independent references.
- GPU output meets foundation tolerances against independent references; combined extremes, migrations, history/restart, stale requests, capability refusal/retry cleanup and MCP parity pass. Historical CPU evidence does not require a second production backend.
- Gestures retain one commit and keyboard cancellation; meet existing SDR interaction gates and record HDR latency separately.

requirements.acceptance:
- Known neutral patches under at least two measured illuminants recover neutrality within a fixed residual tolerance selected during research.
- Tests reject clipped channels, black, transparency, tiny valid regions, and unsupported camera profiles without adding history.
- Cropped, rotated, panned, Fit, and 100% samples identify the same source area within the documented pixel-boundary rule.
- One accepted sample creates one combined edit; Undo/Redo, restart, concurrent MCP edits, Escape, and As Shot pass.
- Keyboard-only use works at 1100 × 700 with the console open, and sampling does not alter originals or display mode.

Full HDR checklist: RAW/bracket/import editing and restart → processing/format/merge owners; controls → operator/mask owners; physical and platform behavior → hdr-display; controlled SDR/output/round trips → format/native-reader owners; exact analysis → analysis-consolidation/legacy-61; memory/performance/recovery/accessibility/MCP → affected owner acceptance and legacy-44. No criterion becomes a pass from migration.

Ratings/keywords/collections, print workflows and unspecified effects are unadopted future candidates; not newly authorized deliverables. Film grain, retouching and depth/FSR have their explicit issues.

Additional formats are the decision-gated next-format outcome. Watermarks and named export presets are unadopted roadmap options, not adopted by this migration. Packaged license/source/relinking conditions remain release acceptance, not a new source-license defect.

Rejected Float32 masks, failed common Rust codec-host candidate, retired camera/reference GPU executors and rejected denoising C16/BM3D remain rejected/research-only; historical GPU-only mandates and aggregate editing goals are superseded by current policy.
